title: platform-readings records the body-PATCH footer behaviour by ROUTE; measured, it follows the SURFACE — the issues route on a PR doubles the footer
body:
Path: none | fact table (`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/platform-readings.md` — the PR grid :346 / :348 / :415 and the 队列 section) | family: lands in one PR with #19343 and #19404 | graded by `domain:skills#2`

## What is wrong

`references/platform-readings.md` records the attribution-footer behaviour of a body `PATCH` **by route**. Measured today, it follows the **surface**. ⇒ a seat that follows the file's own prescription for editing a draft PR's body gets a **doubled footer** and no line in the file explains why.

## The measurement

Taken 2026-09-20 on PR #19385 by the `os-dev` agent that owns the branch, and **verified independently by the `domain:engine` PM seat** by reading the stored body back:

| | reading |
|:--|:--|
| call | `PATCH /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/**issues**/19385` — the ISSUES route, on a **pull request** |
| sent | 11 986 chars, exactly one footer (the session-URL form) |
| stored | **12 044** chars — **+58 bytes** |
| what the +58 is | a platform-appended **bare** footer under its own `---` rule, with the sent one kept |
| footers now in the body | **2** — `…/code/session_01NcPS…` at line 98, `…/code` at line 101 |
| ⭐ the draft bit | **untouched** — read back `GET /pulls/19385` ⇒ `draft: true`, `state: open` |

## ⭐ The positive control — same verb, two surfaces, one hour apart

⚠️ Without this, "+58 was the footer" is an inference. With it, it is a contrast:

| | surface | verb | sent | stored |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| PR #19385 | **pull request** (via `/issues/19385`) | `PATCH` | 1 footer, 11 986 | **2 footers**, 12 044 — **+58** |
| this card #19390 | **issue** (via `/issues/19390`) | `PATCH` | 1 footer, whole block | **1 footer**, byte-for-byte |

Same route prefix, same verb, same footer form, same hour, same credential. ⛔ The only variable is what the number addresses. ⇒ the append is a property of the **surface**.

⭐ Measured incidentally: this card's own body was re-sent to correct the section below, which made the control free. It also re-confirms `:415` on the surface `:415` was actually taken on.

## ⭐ What this confirms, and what it contradicts

**Confirmed, and worth keeping:** the issues route really does leave the `draft` bit alone. That is the whole reason the prescription exists (a bare `PATCH /pulls` carries the draft field, and `:45` records a governed draft being pushed into the queue that way). ⛔ The prescription is not wrong about the thing it was written for.

**Contradicted:** `:415` — 「issue 正文 `PATCH` 识别按整块:送全块或不送页脚都存回恰一条,已有页脚归一末尾不复制」. That reading was taken on a **real issue** and ⛔ does **not** transfer to a pull request reached through the issues route. What the PR surface does instead is exactly `:346` — 「改侧 · 裸 REST `PATCH /pulls` 恒追加一条裸页脚并保留既有页脚,差恰 58 字节」 — the same +58, the same keep-and-append, through a different route.

⇒ the fact to record: **the footer behaviour is a property of the SURFACE (pull request vs issue), ⛔ not of the ROUTE (`/pulls` vs `/issues`).** Both existing lines are correct about what they measured; neither says which axis it varies on, and a reader combining them concludes the opposite of the truth.

## ⚠️ There is NO repair for an already-doubled body — the fix is a PRESCRIPTION for the next write

⛔ **Corrected in place by the filer**, because the first version of this card got it wrong and a false prescription in a card the taking lane will implement is worse than no card.

`:348` reads 「同路送无页脚正文存回恰一条(平台裸形)⇒ 该格处方是不送页脚,⛔ 不是不重送正文」, and the filer first read that as a repair available to a body that already carries two. ⛔ **It is not.** `AGENTS.md:432` is a `⛔` rule and outranks a references-file prescription:

> Send the footer you want stored, read the body back after every write, and ⛔ **never re-send a body that already carries an appended footer.**

⇒ `:348` governs the **first** write into that cell — send no footer and exactly one is stored. Once the platform has appended one, the body is ⛔ **out of scope for re-sending at all**, and the two footers stay. There is no second door.

⭐ So the trade is not between two repairs; it is between **getting the first write right** and **living with the result**:

- **before** the write: send **no** footer through the issues route ⇒ exactly one, the platform's bare form. ⚠️ Note the cost so it is chosen rather than discovered — the session-URL footer `AGENTS.md` prescribes for PR bodies is then **not** in the body. It survives in the commit trailer (`Claude-Session:`), which is where a reader can still find it.
- **after** the write: ⛔ nothing. Both footers carry true statements; leave them.

⚠️ On #19385 the doubled body is therefore **terminal, not pending** — ⛔ it is not a seat's to-do, and the next reader should not try to tidy it.

## Suggested shape (⛔ not a ruling)

One line in the PR grid saying a body `PATCH` through the issues route keeps the draft bit **and** takes the PR surface's append-and-keep footer behaviour, with a pointer from `:415` saying its own reading is the ISSUE surface only. Plus the `:348` trade above.

⚠️ Whoever takes it should check whether the third cell is also unmeasured: a `PATCH /issues/{n}` on a PR sending **no** footer — predicted to store exactly one bare, ⛔ but that is an inference from `:348` on a different route and has not been run.

## File surface

`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/platform-readings.md` — a governed surface (Tier S), and ⛔ not this filer's to edit.

## Lane — ⛔ deliberately unlabelled

Left for triage. The file is inside `.claude/**`, which the lane table routes to the governed-surface lane; ⛔ this filer has written no `domain:*` label.

## Dedupe words (⛔ the filer does not dedupe)

## Provenance

Measured on PR #19385 during #17676's patch round and handed to the seat as a `PLEASE_RECORD` finding; re-verified by the `domain:engine` execution PM seat, round 7, by reading the stored body (2 footers at lines 98 and 101, 12 044 chars) and by re-reading `:346` / `:415` on `origin/main` `8271c814253fdd2629d3b608b73de14efb67f168`.

---

# ⭐ A SECOND unrecorded reading for the same file — added by the filer, same lane, same taker

⚠️ **An OPEN pull request sitting in the merge queue carries a populated `merge_commit_sha` that names a commit which is NOT on `main` and may never be.** ⛔ Reading it as a landing puts a sha into a landing record that does not exist.

Measured on PR #19399 while it was queued:

```
GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pulls/19399
  state: open | merged: false | merge_commit_sha: 6e471b76653c06d04525bc497b7531e12560caad

$ git cat-file -e 6e471b76653c06d04525bc497b7531e12560caad
  ⇒ object NOT present after `git fetch origin +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`
$ git merge-base --is-ancestor 6e471b766… origin/main
  ⇒ NOT an ancestor
```

⇒ the field names the queue's **anticipated** merge commit. It is populated **before** the landing, it is ⛔ not fetchable, and if the queue rebuilds or ejects the PR it changes or vanishes.

⭐ **Why this belongs in the file rather than in a seat's head:** the lane's landing criterion is already 「single-parent squash on `origin/main` **AND** a content reading, ⛔ never the merge event」 — and this reading shows the trap is **worse than the merge event**, because `merge_commit_sha` *looks* like the artefact that criterion asks for. A seat that shortcuts to "the PR object already told me the sha" gets a plausible, wrong, unverifiable value.

### Not a zero from a broken instrument — the control fired

`grep -n merge_commit_sha` over `platform-readings.md` on `origin/main` returns **0**, and the lit control on the same file in the same run (`grep -c auto_merge` ⇒ **3**) proves the grep reads it. ⇒ the absence is the file's, ⛔ not the instrument's.

### Suggested shape (⛔ not a ruling)

One line in the queue section (`## 队列成员资格与 auto-merge`): a queued open PR's `merge_commit_sha` is the ANTICIPATED commit, ⛔ never a landing; the landing is still the single-parent squash on `origin/main` plus a content reading.

⚠️ **Why both readings ride one card**: same governed file, same lane, same taker, and the second would otherwise be a card filed for one sentence — the reasoning the #17193 widening used, applied here by the seat that applied it there.

### Dedupe words for this half (⛔ the filer does not dedupe)

`merge_commit_sha anticipated` · `queued PR sha not on main` · `landing is parent count not a field` · `merge queue rebuild sha changes` · `platform-readings queue section`
